main_body: two-story Japanese machiya building with tiled roof and lattice front
top_band: blue-grey kawara tile roof slope with ridge beam (rows 1-31) plus lower awning roof (rows 41-46)
evidence: Rows 1-31 clearly depict the foreshortened top slope of the main tiled roof with ridge beam and onigawara ornaments; row 29-31 marks the front tile eaves edge, followed by a dark eave shadow at row 32, an upper plaster wall with recessed mushiko-mado windows (rows 33-40), a second foreshortened pent roof (rows 41-46), and a recessed ground-floor facade with wooden lattice, noren curtains, and bamboo inuyarai (rows 48-78).

style.evidence: The roof tiles use a 6-step blue-grey ramp with per-tile highlights and overlap shadows matching the Beodeul roof density. The upper plaster wall has subtle speckling and recessed window frames, and the lower wood lattice, blue noren, and golden bamboo guards have rich multi-step shading and dark material-tinted outlines.
